reasons: Checks are length-only and do not confirm digits.
The sign-in code field has no length cap.
The optional code in the disable step is never used by the service.

terms.meaning: a six-digit code from an authenticator app that changes every 30 seconds
a spare one-time code for signing in when the phone is lost
a short-lived token that proves the password step passed and waits for the second factor

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for two-factor input checks
sections.what: Brings in the rules for text and length, plus the labels used for API docs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same checks style as the other request files.

sections.name: EnableMfaDto
sections.title: Input to confirm two-factor setup
sections.what: Holds the six-digit code from the authenticator app that proves setup worked.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app must see a valid code before it turns two-factor on.
sections.watch_out: Only the length is checked, so letters pass as long as there are six characters.

sections.name: VerifyMfaDto
sections.title: Input to finish sign-in with two-factor
sections.what: Carries the challenge token from password login, the code (authenticator or backup), and optional device details.
sections.why: Likely reason: the second step needs the token from the first step and the code the user typed.
sections.watch_out: The code field has no length limit here, so the service must do the real checking.

sections.name: DisableMfaDto
sections.title: Input to turn off two-factor
sections.what: Requires the account password, with an optional six-digit code for extra confirmation.
sections.why: Likely reason: turning off a security feature should need proof of the account owner.
sections.watch_out: The optional code is accepted but never checked, so the password alone turns off two-factor.

summary: Defines the request shapes for turning two-factor sign-in on, finishing sign-in with it, and turning it off.
purpose: Checks inputs for the two-factor endpoints before the auth service runs.
why: Likely reason: keeps two-factor input checks at the edge of the app. Reason beyond that not stated in the code.
how: Three classes, one per action. Each field has decorators for presence and length. Documentation labels describe each field.
inputs: Request bodies sent to the two-factor endpoints.
outputs: Checked objects for the service, or rejections with error messages.
risks: The code field in the sign-in step accepts text of any length. The code in the enable step checks length but not digits. The optional code in the disable step is accepted but ignored by the service.
debug: If a two-factor request is rejected, read the message for the field name and confirm the code is six characters long.
